components.text: Temporal change allegedly requires God to acquire or lose knowledge and thus undergo intrinsic change.
Classical immutability and pure actuality allegedly preclude any such acquisition or loss.
Explain why temporal changes do not require God to acquire or lose knowledge intrinsically.
Account for God's knowledge of creatures whose existence and temporal predicates change.
The objection treats possession of alternative possibilities as necessary for perfect freedom.
A will fixed on its end allegedly cannot be perfectly free.
Show why inability to do otherwise entails that God's action is not perfectly free.
Reconcile fixed divine ends and absent unrealized potentialities with meaningful freedom.
Natural reason can reach God's existence despite difficulty, with revelation broadening access.
Explain how difficult and uneven access to belief is compatible with a perfectly loving God.
Address whether revelation makes relationship-enabling belief adequately available to every finite person.
The first three ways allegedly converge on a foundational cause of causal reality.
Act-potency causal chains allegedly require termination in a grounding actuality.
The arguments allegedly establish one unique common first cause.
Show that essentially ordered causal series must terminate in a unique first cause.
Explain why interconnected actualizers require one foundational actuality rather than mutual dependence.
Existing things allegedly need an ongoing actualizer rather than merely an originating cause.
The cosmological route relies on presently sustaining causation.
Show why an existing created thing requires continuous actualization rather than merely an originating cause.
Challenge the claim that causal reality must be presently sustained by a foundational cause.
Apparently gratuitous evolutionary suffering is alleged to be improbable under a perfectly good creator.
God is evaluated as though choosing among antecedently available material arrangements.
Justify evaluating a transcendent creator by expectations drawn from ordinary agents acting on preexisting conditions.
Explain why created suffering counts as divine defect or neglect when God creates the whole causal framework.
God's causative knowledge allegedly explains all temporal facts without passive learning.
Past and future entities allegedly receive being from God in a manner sufficient for present knowledge.
Continuous divine causation is invoked as the explanatory model.
Show how causative knowledge can presently concern past or future entities that do not exist.
Resolve the changing-knowledge problem under presentism or growing-block theories of time.
A perfectly good God is evaluated under a moral standard that makes apparently gratuitous suffering evidentially surprising.
The objection assumes divine goodness can be assessed analogously to finite agency.
Perfect goodness allegedly entails relational obligations toward finite persons.
Explain how divine perfect goodness can be assessed without applying a higher moral law to God.
Connect God's status as creator and final end to the goodness relevant to worship and blame.
Changing temporal truths allegedly require succession and alteration in divine knowledge.
Nonexistent past and future events allegedly cannot be equally available to divine causative knowledge.
An immutable God allegedly cannot know subjects whose temporal existence changes.
Explain how all temporal things can be available to divine knowledge despite noneternalist concerns.
Explain how God knows temporal succession without acquiring successive intrinsic states.
The creation framework allegedly changes how suffering and divine neglect should be morally assessed.
Divine goodness allegedly cannot be judged by the same standards applicable to finite makers.
General goods may allegedly justify permitted evil within created reality.
Explain why a creation-level framework answers suffering among nonhuman animals that are not moral agents.
Address whether soul-building or redemptive goods justify extensive prehuman animal suffering.
Perfect love allegedly requires God to secure belief whenever belief is necessary for relationship.
Persistent religious disagreement is alleged to be surprising under perfect loving disclosure.
Nonbelief allegedly precludes the relationship a loving God would promote.
Explain why perfect love need not immediately secure belief for every finite person.
Explain why loving revelation may produce gradual and uneven religious understanding.
Preserve genuine relational availability while allowing nonbelief and non-coercive inquiry.
